title: Override record
$comment: Reframe migration (docs/naming-convention.md, additive): task_correlation_id pattern widened from ^FEAT-\d{4}-\d{4}/T\d{2}$ to ^((FEAT-\d{4}-\d{4})|(INIT-\d{4}-\d{4}/F\d{2}))/T\d{2}$ so a work unit under a dispatched feature (INIT-YYYY-NNNN/FNN/TNN) may own an override, alongside the legacy/component-local FEAT-YYYY-NNNN/TNN form. Existing FEAT- override records validate unchanged. Reconciliation-runtime additions (additive, optional): `repo` (owner/repo to scope reconciliation) and `patch` (unified diff for auto-reapply after a regen) — consumed by scripts/reconcile-overrides.py.
description: A single authorized override of generated code. See orchestrator-architecture.md §9.3 for the reconciliation protocol.

files.description: Paths under the component repo's generated directory that this override modifies.

task_correlation_id.description: Work-unit-level correlation ID of the unit that required the override: INIT-YYYY-NNNN/FNN/TNN (work unit under a dispatched feature) or the legacy/component-local FEAT-YYYY-NNNN/TNN. See docs/naming-convention.md.

tracking_issue.description: GitHub issue that retires the override when closed, in `owner/repo#number` form.

expiry_condition.description: Human-readable condition under which this override is retired. Typically `on closure of <tracking_issue>` but may be broader.

timestamp.description: When the override was authorized (ISO 8601 with timezone).

repo.description: Optional `owner/repo` of the component repo this override lives in. Lets the reconciliation runtime (scripts/reconcile-overrides.py) scope to the repo just regenerated and locate its checkout. If absent, the runtime processes the record against every involved repo.

patch.description: Optional unified diff (git apply format) that re-applies the override to the regenerated file(s). When present, the reconciliation runtime auto-reapplies it after a regen (emitting override_applied); when absent, the runtime flags the override for manual reapply (blocked_spec) since the metadata alone cannot reconstruct the change. Future: once the generator reads the registry (architecture §9.3 future model), this becomes the source the generator respects.
